message.content: {"caption":"A workflow diagram shows rollout traces being analyzed into patches and merged into an evolved skill.","description":"The diagram flows from left to right. A purple geometric skill symbol and crossed-tools symbol, joined by an × and labeled “Rollout Using Skills,” point by an arrow into a dashed rounded box labeled “Traces.” Inside are three stacked trace cards: a green “Success Trace” reading “Agent successfully matched rows across two sheets.” with a green circled check; a red “Error Trace” reading “MEDIAN(IF(xxx))” returned None in recalc.py, with a red circled X; and a red “Error Trace” reading “recalc.py” can't handle excel array formulas., also with a red circled X. The cards carry magenta τ+ and τ− markers, respectively. Each trace points right to a purple geometric analysis symbol, marked A+ for the success trace and A− for each error trace, then onward to its corresponding patch. A dashed rounded group labeled “Patches” contains three cards: the green “Addition” card, “Patch1: add new pattern from success trace,” lists “Cast ID columns to str,” “Cast numeric columns to float before,” and “Cross-sheet row matching to prevent silent type-mismatch failures.” The light-red “Addition” card, “Patch2: add new warning from error trace,” lists “Array formulas silently fail in LibreOffice” and “Pre-calculate in Python and write the result as a literal value instead.” The pale-red “Edition” card, “Patch3: Deepening existing rules from error trace,” lists “Use formulas, not hardcoded values.”, “Same rule, now with explicit text-function,” and “Add warning against auto-applying .strip”. Arrows carry the top and bottom patches along bent paths into the purple “Merge Patches” symbol (from above and below, respectively); the middle patch points directly into it. A final rightward arrow leads to crossed tools topped by a gold crown, labeled “Evolved Skill.”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
